claims.quote: rarities (e.g., a mermaid's hand, a dragon's egg, two feathers of a phoenix's tail, a piece of the True Cross, and a vial of blood that rained in the Isle of Wight)

claims.claim: The earliest pictorial record of a natural history cabinet shows a crocodile suspended from the ceiling
claims.quote: Every surface of the vaulted ceiling is occupied with preserved fishes, stuffed mammals and curious shells, with a stuffed crocodile suspended in the centre.

claims.claim: Ferrante Imperato's 1599 engraving is the earliest pictorial record of a natural history cabinet
claims.quote: The earliest pictorial record of a natural history cabinet is the engraving in Ferrante Imperato's Dell'Historia Naturale (Naples 1599)

claims.claim: Fishes and shells cover the vault in the engraving
claims.quote: Every surface of the vaulted ceiling is occupied with preserved fishes, stuffed mammals and curious shells

claims.claim: Coins, shells and a Madonna image appear together on one table
claims.quote: Archive title: File:Frans Francken the Younger - The cabinet of a collector with paintings, shells, coins, fossils and flowers - 1619.jpg — and in the image coins and shells lie on the table with a panel of the Adoration of the Magi (Madonna and Child) propped on it

claims.claim: "Cabinet" first meant a room, not a piece of furniture
claims.quote: The term cabinet originally described a room rather than a piece of furniture.

claims.claim: The categories these objects would be sorted into had not yet been defined
claims.quote: encyclopedic collections of objects whose categorical boundaries were, in Renaissance Europe, yet to be defined

claims.quote: Date: 1619 ... Author: Frans Francken the Younger ... Licence: Public domain

claims.claim: Clockwork objects sat beside tusks, skeletons and minerals in these cabinets
claims.quote: These seventeenth-century cabinets were filled with preserved animals, horns, tusks, skeletons, minerals, as well as other interesting man-made objects: sculptures wondrously old, wondrously fine or wondrously small; clockwork automata

claims.claim: Worm's collection held a "Scythian Lamb", a woolly fern thought to be part plant, part sheep
claims.quote: Worm's collection contained, for example, what he thought was a Scythian Lamb, a woolly fern thought to be a plant/sheep fabulous creature.

claims.claim: The Tradescant collection became the Ashmolean Museum
claims.quote: Ashmole's donation formed the foundation of the Ashmolean Museum at Oxford.

claims.claim: Ashmole bought the Ark in 1659
claims.quote: Ashmole, a collector in his own right, acquired the Tradescant Ark in 1659

claims.claim: Ashmole gave the collection to Oxford in 1675
claims.quote: In 1675, he donated his library and collection and the Tradescant collection to the University of Oxford

claims.claim: The green cupboard photograph is by Fredrik Andersson, Skokloster Castle, public domain
claims.quote: Author: Fredrik Andersson Licence: Public domain ... Skoklosters slott

claims.claim: A cabinet of curiosities was a private room
claims.quote: The term cabinet originally described a room rather than a piece of furniture.

claims.claim: The classic cabinets appeared in sixteenth-century Europe
claims.quote: Although more rudimentary collections had preceded them, the classic cabinets of curiosities emerged in the sixteenth century.

claims.claim: John Tradescant the Elder and his son filled a cabinet in South Lambeth and opened it to the public for a small entrance fee
claims.quote: By the 1630s, the Tradescants displayed their eclectic collection at their residence in South Lambeth. Tradescant's Ark, as it came to be known, was the earliest major cabinet of curiosity in England and open to the public for a small entrance fee.

claims.claim: The 1656 catalogue was financed by their neighbour Elias Ashmole
claims.quote: Ashmole was also a neighbor of the Tradescants in Lambeth. He financed the publication of Musaeum Tradescantianum, a catalogue of the Ark collection in 1656.

claims.claim: The catalogue listed a dodo and a walrus jaw
claims.quote: collected zoological (e.g., the dodo from Mauritius, the upper jaw of a walrus, and armadillos)

claims.claim: The collection included a vial of blood that rained on the Isle of Wight
claims.quote: a vial of blood that rained in the Isle of Wight

claims.claim: Ashmole's 1675 gift was made on condition that a building be provided
claims.quote: provided that a suitable building be provided to house the collection

claims.claim: Hans Sloane's collection was bequeathed to England for £20,000 in 1753 and became the British Museum
claims.quote: Upon his death in 1753, Sloane bequeathed his sizable collection of 337 volumes to England for £20,000. In 1759, George II's royal library was added to Sloane's collection to form the foundation of the British Museum.

claims.claim: By the early eighteenth century Enlightenment thinkers had turned against curiosities, treating rarities as misleading exceptions to nature's uniformity
claims.quote: As Enlightenment thinkers placed growing emphasis on patterns and systems within nature, anomalies and rarities came to be regarded as potentially misleading objects of study. Curiosities ... were increasingly seen as vulgar exceptions to nature's overall uniformity.
